n_c2s1_intro.text: The king's messengers came up to Bethlehem, to the house of Jesse, with a word from Saul.

1sam16_19.text: Therefore Saul sent messengers to Jesse, and said, “Send me David your son, who is with the sheep.”

n_c2s1_flock.text: But the flock was still his. He could not go until another man could keep it.

n_c2s1_keeper.text: A hired man was waiting at the day fold, to keep the flock while he was gone.

n_c2s1_names.text: A keeper who cannot tell them apart cannot tell which is missing. So he showed him the ones that answer to a name.

n_c2s1_count.text: Nine went under the rod, and the keeper counted them after him.

n_c2s1_well.text: He showed him the well: where to lever the stone, and how much the trough must hold.

n_c2s1_handed.text: The flock was another man's to keep now, for the first morning he could remember.

1sam16_20.text: Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, and a bottle of wine, and a young goat, and sent them by David his son to Saul.

n_c2s1_gift.text: A father does not send his son before a king with empty hands.

n_c2s1_leave.text: He took the halter and went up the ridge road toward Gibeah, a shepherd sent to serve a king.

n_c2s2_intro.text: From Bethlehem the road to Gibeah runs north along the ridge: half a day, with a loaded donkey.

n_c2s2_load.text: Bread, a bottle of wine and a young goat: his house's word to the king. It had to arrive whole.

n_c2s2_jebus.text: Beside the road Jebus stood walled on its hill: a strong city, and not Israel's. A traveller here had once said of it:

judg19_12.text: His master said to him, “We won’t enter into the city of a foreigner that is not of the children of Israel; but we will pass over to Gibeah.”

n_c2s2_on.text: He did not turn in. He went on toward Gibeah.

n_c2s2_dusk.text: Toward evening, where the road drops between the rocks, the wolves came down.

n_c2s2_gibeah.text: And as the light went, Gibeah of Saul stood above him.

n_c2s2_whole.text: The bread, the wine and the young goat had come whole.

n_c2s3_intro.text: The sun was on the hills when he came under the wall of Gibeah, the donkey behind him and nothing lost from its load.

n_c2s3_shut.text: The gate was already barred for the night.

n_c2s3_keeper.text: Before it stood a man who had turned away better than a shepherd boy that day.

n_c2s3_no.text: “The king has sent for you? Then the king can send for you again in the morning.”

n_c2s3_ask.text: He asked for the one who had spoken of him, and the gatekeeper sent a boy running.

1sam16_18.text: Then one of the young men answered and said, “Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite who is skillful in playing, a mighty man of valor, a man of war, prudent in speech, and a handsome person; and the LORD is with him.”

n_c2s3_open.text: The young man looked at him, and at the lyre, and said, “This is he.” The bar was lifted.

n_c2s3_yard.text: Inside, the yard was going blue with evening. The gift was the steward’s to receive, at the storehouse across the yard.

n_c2s3_cistern.text: The cistern, the storehouse, the door of the hall: he learned the place as he crossed it.

n_c2s3_jonathan.text: On the wall stood a young man with a bow, watching the yard as one who answered for it: Jonathan, the king’s son.

n_c2s3_unmet.text: He looked once at the shepherd boy, and the boy at him. Neither spoke. That day was still to come.

n_c2s3_steward.text: The steward had been on his feet since before light, with a tally still to finish.

n_c2s3_morning.text: “Tie it by the wall. I will see to it in the morning.”

n_c2s3_received.text: Bread, wine and the young goat: he took each from the boy’s hands and marked his tally.

n_c2s3_whole.text: What his father sent had come whole into the king’s house.

n_c2s3_wait.text: At the hall door the young man said, “Wait here. When he asks for you, I will come.”

n_c2s3_called.text: So he sat by the door with the lyre across his knees, while the lamps were lit inside, and waited.

n_c2s4_intro.text: When the lamps were lit the young man came for him. The hall was quiet as a house is quiet when no one dares to speak.

n_c2s4_servants.text: The king's own servants had asked for this. They had said to him:

1sam16_16.text: “Let our lord now command your servants who are in front of you to seek out a man who is a skillful player on the harp. Then when the evil spirit from God is on you, he will play with his hand, and you will be well.”

1sam16_21a.text: David came to Saul, and stood before him.

n_c2s4_shadow.text: The king did not look up. On the wall behind him his shadow stood taller than one lamp could make it.

n_c2s4_song.text: No one told him what to play. He had one song of his own, made a line at a time in the hills.

n_c2s4_turn.text: The king turned his face to the wall. The steward touched the boy's shoulder: “Wait a little. Then begin again.”

n_c2s4_rest.text: The king's hands opened. He leaned back and breathed like a man asleep after a long watch. On the wall was only the shadow of a man sitting by a lamp.

1sam16_23.text: When the spirit from God was on Saul, David took the harp, and played with his hand; so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.

1sam16_22.text: Saul sent to Jesse, saying, “Please let David stand before me; for he has found favor in my sight.”

n_c2s4_kept.text: He had come for one evening. He was not sent home.

n_c2s5_intro.text: Days went by in the fortress at Gibeah, and a boy who is kept in a king's house is given work.

n_c2s5_serve.text: No one in the yard asked what he could do with a sling. They asked for water.

n_c2s5_water.text: The cistern was deep and the rope was long. He knew this work.

n_c2s5_oil.text: The steward measured out the oil as if it were his own, and gave it.

n_c2s5_lamps.text: The lamps of the hall were filled before the king woke. No one remarked on it. That was how he knew it was done well.

n_c2s5_drillsee.text: In the yard an old soldier with a padded pole was drilling the king's young guards, teaching them not to flinch. David had water to carry.

n_c2s5_days.text: So it went, day after day.

n_c2s5_word.text: Then one morning the young man who had spoken for him came out of the hall with a word from the king, for David to carry.

n_c2s5_arms.text: The steward brought them out himself: the king's shield and the king's spear. They were heavier than they looked, and not his.

1sam16_21b.text: He loved him greatly; and he became his armor bearer.

n_c2s5_place.text: He stood at the king's door with them through the heat of the day. Men went in and out. None looked at the boy. They looked to see that the shield was there.

n_c2s5_called.text: On the third morning the old shield-man beckoned him over. An arm that carries the king's shield, he said, must put it between the king and a blow.

n_c2s5_done.text: The old man grounded his pole and nodded once. It was all the praise there was.

n_c2s5_untested.text: He had learned to raise a shield for another man. He had not learned to wear a king's armour, and no one had asked it.

n_c2s5_end.text: He carried them back to the king's door. He had been anointed to be king, and he was holding another man's spear. He held it well.

n_c2s6_intro.text: It did not stay away. Some nights it came back, worse than in the evening. They woke him in the dark and brought him to the hall.

1sam16_14.text: Now Yahweh’s Spirit departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from Yahweh troubled him.

n_c2s6_alone.text: The servants would not go in at night. There was the king, the lamps, and one boy with a lyre.

n_c2s6_before.text: The king sat as on the first evening, and did not look up. The shadow behind him reached the beams.

n_c2s6_spear.text: The king’s spear stood in its place by his seat, as it did every night.

n_c2s6_lull.text: The king’s shoulders came down a little. Then the wind found the hall, and the lamps began to fail. In the dark it would come back sooner.

n_c2s6_turn.text: The king turned his face to the wall. There was no one to tell the boy to wait, so he waited. He lit the lamps again, and when the king’s breathing slowed he began again.

n_c2s6_rest.text: Past the middle of the night it let go of him. The king slept in his seat with his head against the wall, and the lamps burned straight.

n_c2s6_song.text: He played on softly, and then stopped. The quiet stayed in the room after the lyre was still. It had not done that before.

n_c2s6_end.text: He sat by the lamp until it was light under the door. No one had seen it done, and in the morning no one spoke of it.

n_c2s7_intro.text: When the king was well there was no work at Gibeah for a harpist, and his father's sheep were still his father's. So he went home to them, and came again when he was sent for.

n_c2s7_light.text: He set out at first light with no donkey and no load: only staff, sling and lyre.

n_c2s7_jebus.text: Jebus stood on its hill in the early light. He passed under it as before.

n_c2s7_wolves.text: Above the ford a man had left his sheep by the road, each daubed red on the rump, and no one with them. The wolves had found that out first.

n_c2s7_kept.text: They were not his father's sheep. He had not stopped to ask whose they were.

n_c2s7_home.text: By the middle of the morning Bethlehem lay below him, and the smoke of his father's house.

n_c2s7_jesse.text: His father asked after the king, and then sent him to look at the sheep, as he had known he would.

n_c2s7_keeper.text: The keeper had them in the day fold: nine, as he had been given nine. He had counted them every evening, and was proud of it.

n_c2s7_count.text: Nine went under the rod. The count was whole.

n_c2s7_eight.text: Shai came to his voice, and Rachel, and Noga. He called Devorah, and nothing in the fold lifted its head. Nine by the rod; eight by name.

n_c2s7_stranger.text: Under the dust on her rump was a daub of red, nearly worn away: the ford man's ewe. She had come in with the nine one evening, and the count had hidden it: one too many and one too few still make nine.

n_c2s7_where.text: The keeper had done what he was hired to do. Devorah had been gone for days, and no one had known to look. But a lost ewe goes back to where she has always slept.

n_c2s7_devorah.text: She was in the night fold by the house, where she had slept every night of her life, behind a bar no one had come to lift.

n_c2s7_nine.text: Now there were nine of his father's in the fold, and one that was not.

n_c2s7_water.text: He drew for them himself, and watched each one drink.

n_c2s7_night.text: That evening he sat by the fold and played to them, as on the hills. What he had learned in the king's hall at night held after his hand was still: they lay quiet until morning.

n_c2s7_morning.text: In the morning he gave the nine back to the keeper, and this time the keeper said the four names himself. The red ewe he would take: the ford was on his road.

n_c2s7_voice.text: She did not know his voice and would not come to it. But she would follow the lyre.

n_c2s7_leave.text: His father came to the gate. He did not ask when he would be back. It had become the way of things: the king's house, the fold, and the road between.

n_c2s7_north.text: So he went up the ridge road again, at a strange ewe's pace.

n_c2s7_runner.text: A man came down the road toward him at a run, and did not slow or speak.

n_c2s7_given.text: At the fold above the ford she smelled her own and went in to them unplayed. The ford man was out with the rest. He would count that night and find it right, and never know it had been wrong.

n_c2s7_news.text: Under Jebus there were more of them, running south to rouse Judah, and what they called out as they passed was war.

n_c2s7_called.text: Every man of Israel who could bear arms was being called out.

n_c2s7_west.text: From the height the land fell away westward, ridge after ridge, toward a valley he could not see. Socoh lay that way, and the valley of Elah.

n_c2s7_end.text: He was the king's harpist and armour-bearer, and his father's shepherd, and he went on up the road. And so it was, while the armies gathered:

1sam17_1.text: Now the Philistines gathered together their armies to battle; and they were gathered together at Socoh, which belongs to Judah, and encamped between Socoh and Azekah, in Ephesdammim.

1sam17_15.text: Now David went back and forth from Saul to feed his father’s sheep at Bethlehem.
